fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. The men from Bethel ask the priests of the house of the LORD of Hosts, and the prophets too (Zechariah 7:3). They sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, along with their men, so this wasn't a casual question over the fence. Their question was about weeping and fasting in the fifth month.

Good guess if you're picturing a government office, but that's not where they go. The text says they ask the priests of the house of the LORD of Hosts, as well as the prophets (Zechariah 7:3). The governor never shows up in this verse. The question goes to the priests and the prophets.

Close to home, but that's not who they ask. The men sent from Bethel bring their question to the priests of the house of the LORD of Hosts and to the prophets (Zechariah 7:3). No town elders appear in these verses. The ones they ask are the priests and the prophets.

Not quite, friend. The text doesn't bring up the priests approving anything. God asks the people, "…was it really for Me that you fasted?" (Zechariah 7:5). The question goes straight to the reason behind the fasting.
Good thought, but the verse says something else. God proclaimed these words through the earlier prophets (Zechariah 7:7). Kings aren't the ones named here. The words came through the prophets.
This one's actually true, friend. The LORD of Hosts says, "Administer true justice." (Zechariah 7:9). It leads off His list of what to do. Straight and plain, with no loopholes.

That's the word. God says, "Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor." (Zechariah 7:10). He names four groups, and nobody is left guessing who He means. To oppress means to press down on someone, and He says don't.

Not that one, friend. The verse says, "Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor." (Zechariah 7:10). The command isn't about being afraid of anyone. It's about not pressing down on these four groups.

Not that one, friend. The verse says, "Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor." (Zechariah 7:10). Oppress is a heavier word than blame. It means pressing down on someone, and God says don't do it to these four.

That's right. The LORD says He scattered them "…with a whirlwind among all the nations that they had not known…" (Zechariah 7:14). These were nations they had not known. I think that's a hard way to be scattered.

Not this time, friend. The verse says the LORD scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations that they had not known (Zechariah 7:14). That's nations, not the towns of Judah. I think this is a heavy verse.

That's a famous spot, but it's not in this verse. The LORD says He scattered them "…with a whirlwind among all the nations that they had not known…" (Zechariah 7:14). The text points to nations, not to a wilderness. I think this is a heavy verse.
